description: External ear anatomy: helix, antihelix, tragus, lobule, ear axis, projection. Dimensions are drawn from craniofacial anthropometry (Farkas) and otoplasty literature (McDowell, Mustardé, Furnas). The earlobe attachment dimension (free/attached/intermediate) is the canonical Mendelian-genetics teaching example, though contemporary research has shown the trait is more polygenic and continuous than the textbook treatment suggests.

dimensions.scale_citation: Aligned with otoplasty-literature descriptors of helical-rim morphology.
dimensions.description: Curvature and prominence of the helix (the outer rim of the ear).

values.definition: Smooth, continuous helical curve from superior to lobule.
Reduced curve at the superior helix; common otoplasty correction target.
Third crus visible; abnormal cartilage fold creating a pointed superior helix.
Furled or rolled helical rim creating a cupped appearance.
Notable left-right helical morphology difference.

observability.notes: Best assessed from lateral or three-quarter view; frontal view captures only ear protrusion.

dimensions.scale_citation: Mustardé JC (1963). The correction of prominent ears using simple mattress sutures. British Journal of Plastic Surgery, 16. Antihelix-fold definition is the central otoplasty-correction landmark.
dimensions.description: Definition of the antihelical fold. Loss of antihelix definition is the primary cause of prominent ears.

values.definition: Clear antihelical fold; ear lies close to head.
Antihelix visible but fold not crisp.
Antihelical fold absent or substantially reduced; ear appears to project from head.

dimensions.scale_citation: Furnas DW (1968). Correction of prominent ears by concha-mastoid sutures. Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery, 42(3). Reference: auriculo-cephalic angle ~20-25° aesthetic norm.
dimensions.description: Angle between the ear and the side of the head, captured ordinally.

values.definition: Auriculo-cephalic angle below ~15°; ear barely projects from head.
Angle approximately 15-25°.
Angle 25-35°; visibly prominent.
Angle >35°; pronounced ear protrusion ('lop ear' / 'cup ear' in extreme cases).

observability.notes: Best assessed from frontal or posterior view; lateral view alone underestimates protrusion.

dimensions.scale_citation: Shaffer JR et al. (2017). Genome-wide association study reveals multiple loci influencing normal human earlobe attachment. American Journal of Human Genetics, 101(6). The classic Mendelian-genetics two-state classification is now understood as a polygenic continuum; this scale uses three buckets reflecting that continuum.
dimensions.description: Degree of attachment of the earlobe to the side of the head. Classically taught as two-state (free/attached) but contemporary genetics work demonstrates a continuous distribution; three buckets capture the meaningful variation.

values.definition: Earlobe hangs free of the head; clear gap between lobule and adjacent skin.
Partial attachment; lobule attaches to head along part of its edge but not fully.
Lobule attaches to head along its entire posterior edge; no free hanging.

dimensions.scale_citation: Aligned with descriptors used in otoplasty and forensic-anthropology literature.

values.definition: Limited lobule mass; minimal hanging tissue.
Average lobule size.
Pronounced lobule mass; large hanging tissue.
Lobule visibly stretched from gauge piercings or repeated heavy earrings; native size not assessable.

dimensions.scale_citation: Otologic anatomy descriptors aligned with otologic-surgery references.
dimensions.description: Shape of the tragus (the small projection anterior to the ear canal).

values.definition: One distinct tragal projection.
Two visible projections; common variant.
Tragus visible but rounded rather than pointed.
Tragus barely visible; small or recessed.

dimensions.scale_citation: Farkas LG (1994). Anthropometry of the Head and Face, 2nd Edition. Reference: ear axis approximately 15-20° posterior tilt from vertical.
dimensions.description: Inclination of the long ear axis relative to vertical, viewed laterally.

values.definition: Ear axis nearly vertical.
Within Farkas reference range.
Pronounced backward inclination.

dimensions.scale_citation: Farkas LG (1994). Reference: total ear height approximately equal to nasal length in European-population aesthetic norm.
dimensions.description: Overall ear length proportional to face.

values.definition: Ear length below population median.
Average ear length.
Ear length above population median; common with aging (ears continue growing through life).

references: Farkas LG (1994). Anthropometry of the Head and Face, 2nd Edition. Raven Press.
Mustardé JC (1963). The correction of prominent ears using simple mattress sutures. British Journal of Plastic Surgery, 16: 170-178.
Furnas DW (1968). Correction of prominent ears by concha-mastoid sutures. Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery, 42(3): 189-193.
Shaffer JR, Li J, Lee MK, et al. (2017). Genome-wide association study reveals multiple loci influencing normal human earlobe attachment. American Journal of Human Genetics, 101(6): 913-924.
McDowell AJ (1968). Goals in otoplasty for protruding ears. Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery, 41(1).
